title: Growth Parameters — Weight, Length, Head Circumference
sources: Critical Vector — Neonatology Pocket Guide: Growth Parameters
WHO growth standards (0–2 y); CDC growth charts (> 2 y)

changelog.change: Initial entry — expected trajectories for weight / length / head circumference, the growth-disorder differential by parameter, and the red flags.

purpose: Expected growth trajectories and the thresholds that should prompt evaluation. Plot on a standardised chart and judge the TREND over time, not a single point — use the same chart consistently for a given child.
ageRange: Birth to ~2 years (WHO); older children use CDC charts

rows: Lose up to 7–10% of birth weight (physiologic)
Triple birth weight by 1 year; quadruple by ~ 2 years

body.text: The doubling/tripling rules are teaching approximations, not a percentile standard — plot on the WHO chart for the actual assessment.

items: Birth ~ 50 cm; 1 year ~ 75 cm (1.5× birth length); 4 years ~ 100 cm (2× birth length).
After age 4: ~ 5–6 cm/year until puberty, then a peak-puberty spurt of ~ 8–12 cm/year.

body.text: Brain growth is fastest in the first 2 years then slows sharply — HC is not a 'doubling' parameter. Plot on an HC-for-age chart.

rows: Poor weight gain / failure to thrive
Inadequate intake / malnutrition, IUGR, chronic GI/renal/cardiac/pulmonary disease, syndromic (Down, Turner), hypothyroidism, malignancy, psychosocial deprivation
Familial; constitutional delay; Turner, achondroplasia; GH deficiency, hypothyroidism; chronic disease
Genetic; congenital (TORCH) infection; perinatal hypoxic injury; malnutrition; craniosynostosis
Hydrocephalus; benign familial macrocephaly; tumour; metabolic storage disease; subdural collection

body.text: Red flags: crossing down ≥ 2 major percentile lines; height < 3rd or > 97th percentile; no weight gain (or weight loss) over an interval where gain is expected; falling growth velocity; growth failure with developmental delay or signs of systemic disease.

buildNote: Trajectories per classical paediatric teaching; plotting standard is WHO 0–2 y / CDC > 2 y.
